articles.title: Badenoch unveils plan to end £100,000 childcare 'cliff edge' ahead of Tory conference
articles.summary: The Conservative leader tells the BBC the earnings threshold for government support stops people "working harder".
articles.content:
Kemi Badenoch has said a Conservative government would scrap the "cliff edge" that mean parents in England lose out on childcare support when they earn more than £100,000 a year.

Speaking to the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg, the Conservative Party leader said: "What we want to see is that people who work harder don't get punished for doing so."

Under the current system, only families where no parent earns more than this threshold are eligible for government-funded or tax-free childcare.

The announcement comes as Conservative members gather for the party's annual conference in Birmingham.

Badenoch, who arrived in the city on Saturday, has vowed the party was new and different from the one that lost the 2024 general election.

The Conservatives - who have been polling behind Labour and Reform UK over the past year - are expected to use the four-day event to lay out more of its policy agenda ahead of the next general election.

Ahead of the conference, the Conservatives produced a 100-page essay setting out their principles including a "central" belief that business, rather than governments, create growth.

It argues that governments should create the conditions for growth, particularly through the tax system.

During her interview, Badenoch insisted the Tories would keep the state pension triple lock, which Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to change if Labour wins the next election.

She said the policy, under which state pensions rise each year by the highest of inflation, average wages, or 2.5%, was "the right policy for pensioners".

She added: "What we don't want to see is people going after the elderly, chasing after vulnerable and disabled people, and then the extremely large cohort of people who can work, who are not working, are left alone."

The Conservatives have long called on the government to cut the growing welfare budget including by implementing tighter restrictions on claimants.

articles.personality_title: Conservatives plan to remove childcare support limit for parents earning over £100,000
articles.personality_presentation:
**Context** – In England, parents who earn more than £100,000 a year currently lose access to government help with childcare costs. This rule creates a sharp cutoff, meaning families just above this income level get no support, which some say discourages people from earning more.

**What happened** – Kemi Badenoch, leader of the Conservative Party, announced plans to end this childcare support cutoff. She said the government wants parents who work harder and earn more to keep receiving help, instead of losing it all once they pass the £100,000 mark. Badenoch shared this news during an interview before the Conservative Party’s annual conference in Birmingham.

**Impact** – Removing this limit could make childcare more affordable for many families who currently lose support when their income slightly exceeds £100,000. This change encourages parents to earn more without fearing losing financial help for childcare. It also shows a shift in Conservative policies as they prepare for the next general election.

**What's next step** – The Conservative Party will likely include this childcare support change in their policy plans at the upcoming conference. If they win the next election, they may introduce this as a new government rule to support working families.

**One-sentence takeaway** – The Conservative Party plans to remove the £100,000 income cutoff for childcare support to help more working parents afford childcare and encourage higher earnings.
articles.personality_title_fr: Les conservateurs veulent supprimer la limite de 100 000 £ pour l’aide à la garde d’enfants
articles.personality_presentation_fr:
**Contexte** – En Angleterre, les parents gagnant plus de 100 000 £ par an perdent actuellement l’aide gouvernementale pour la garde d’enfants. Cette règle crée un seuil net, ce qui signifie que les familles juste au-dessus de ce revenu ne reçoivent aucun soutien, ce qui décourage certains de gagner plus.

**Ce qui s’est passé** – Kemi Badenoch, cheffe du Parti conservateur, a annoncé son intention de supprimer ce seuil pour l’aide à la garde d’enfants. Elle a déclaré que le gouvernement souhaite que les parents qui travaillent plus dur et gagnent plus continuent à recevoir de l’aide, au lieu de tout perdre une fois le seuil de 100 000 £ dépassé. Badenoch a partagé cette nouvelle lors d’une interview avant la conférence annuelle du Parti conservateur à Birmingham.

**Impact** – Supprimer cette limite pourrait rendre la garde d’enfants plus abordable pour de nombreuses familles qui perdent actuellement leur soutien dès que leur revenu dépasse légèrement 100 000 £. Ce changement encourage les parents à gagner plus sans craindre de perdre l’aide financière pour la garde d’enfants. Cela montre aussi une évolution des politiques conservatrices en vue des prochaines élections générales.

**Prochaine étape** – Le Parti conservateur devrait inclure ce changement dans ses plans politiques lors de la prochaine conférence. S’ils remportent les élections, ils pourraient introduire cette règle pour mieux soutenir les familles qui travaillent.

**Résumé en une phrase** – Le Parti conservateur prévoit de supprimer la limite de 100 000 £ pour l’aide à la garde d’enfants afin d’aider plus de parents travailleurs à payer la garde d’enfants et encourager des revenus plus élevés.
articles.personality_title_es: Los conservadores planean eliminar el límite de 100 000 £ para la ayuda infantil
articles.personality_presentation_es:
**Contexto** – En Inglaterra, los padres que ganan más de 100 000 £ al año actualmente pierden el apoyo del gobierno para el cuidado de los hijos. Esta regla crea un límite claro, lo que significa que las familias justo por encima de este ingreso no reciben ayuda, lo que desanima a algunos a ganar más.

**Qué pasó** – Kemi Badenoch, líder del Partido Conservador, anunció planes para eliminar este límite en la ayuda para el cuidado infantil. Dijo que el gobierno quiere que los padres que trabajan más duro y ganan más sigan recibiendo ayuda, en lugar de perderla toda al superar las 100 000 £. Badenoch compartió esta noticia durante una entrevista antes de la conferencia anual del Partido Conservador en Birmingham.

**Impacto** – Quitar este límite podría hacer que el cuidado infantil sea más barato para muchas familias que actualmente pierden apoyo cuando sus ingresos superan ligeramente las 100 000 £. Este cambio anima a los padres a ganar más sin miedo a perder ayuda financiera para el cuidado de sus hijos. También muestra un cambio en las políticas conservadoras de cara a las próximas elecciones generales.

**Próximo paso** – Es probable que el Partido Conservador incluya este cambio en sus planes políticos en la próxima conferencia. Si ganan las elecciones, podrían introducir esta nueva norma para apoyar mejor a las familias trabajadoras.

**Resumen en una frase** – El Partido Conservador planea eliminar el límite de ingresos de 100 000 £ para la ayuda al cuidado infantil para ayudar a más padres trabajadores a pagar el cuidado infantil y fomentar mayores ingresos.
